question.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $5$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{8x-3}{5x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{8x-3}{5(x+1/5)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{8x-3}{(x+1/5)}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

|  | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $-\frac{1}{5}$ | $8$ | $-3$ |
|  | $↓$ | $-\frac{8}{5}$ |
|  | $8$ | $-\frac{23}{5}$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8x-3}{(x+1/5)} & =8-\frac{(23/5)}{(x+1/5)} \\  & =8-\frac{23}{5x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{8x-3}{5x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}(8-\frac{23}{5x+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[8{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x-23{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{5x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{[8x-\frac{23}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡|5x+1|]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[8(1-0)-\frac{23}{5}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|6|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|1|)] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[8-\frac{23\operatorname{ln}⁡6}{5}] \\  & =\frac{8}{5}-\frac{23}{25}\operatorname{ln}⁡(6).\end{aligned}
$$
